chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Murāzim, who said:

Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: “May Allah set you aright, I have many supererogatory prayers upon me; so what should I do?” He said: “Make them up.” He said to him: “They are more than that.” He said: “Make them up.” He said: “I cannot count them.” He said: “Estimate.”

Murāzim said: “And I had been ill for four months during which I did not perform supererogatory prayers. So I said: ‘May Allah set you aright, or may I be made your ransom, I was ill for four months in which I did not perform any nāfilah.’ He said: ‘There is no making up upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy one. Everything over which Allah has overcome him, then Allah is more entitled to excuse him in it.’”

Al-Shaykh رحمه الله said: “Whoever turns around in an obligatory salat (prayer) until he sees whoever is behind him, repeating the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him. The following indicates that.”

key_terms.اقْضِهَا: make them up as missed devotional acts
key_terms.الْعُذْرِ: a valid excuse that removes liability
key_terms.الْمَرِيضَ: the sick person whose condition affects legal responsibility
key_terms.تَوَخَّ: estimate to the best of your judgment when the exact number is unknown
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: compensatory performance of a missed act of worship
key_terms.نَوَافِلَ: supererogatory prayers beyond the obligatory salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Do missed nāfilah prayers need to be made up, and is there qaḍāʾ for them if they were missed due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on making up missed nāfilah prayers, instructing a person to perform their qaḍāʾ and, if unable to count them, to estimate them. It also distinguishes the case of illness, stating that missed supererogatory prayers during sickness do not require qaḍāʾ, because one overpowered by a condition decreed by Allah is excused.
